attributes.residual: MIXED and PARKED, but for a materially better-understood reason than the superseded record gave. (A) SHORT SIDE, 9 tokens, NOW CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT AT ALL THREE SITES: two distinct source spellings were probed against the two distinct micro-shapes and BOTH came back byte-identical, establishing that MWCC canonicalises every guard spelling to the single inverted branch and that the forward branch pair is NOT reachable from a guard whose body targets an INTERIOR label, however that guard is written. The binding precondition is the DE law's epilogue target, not the empty-block law's weaker 'block reached from elsewhere' (which all three of these sites already satisfy). Peephole was verified genuinely OFF for this TU first (cflags_demo rewrites -O4,p to -O4), so the surviving pair in the target is NOT a peephole-flag difference and no flag change is owed. Banked as a law. (B) LONG SIDE, 3 tokens: @79c is now DIAGNOSED, not merely censused -- the target loads wobj->flags ONCE into r3 and reuses it across the branch for both the rlwinm. test and the oris, while ours loads it, materialises an address temp `addi r17,r19,16`, and RELOADS it, because the source spells ONE field TWO ways (`((WorldObj*)wobj)->flags` for the test, a raw offsetof cast for the store). The single-spelling cached-load cure DOES remove the reload -- that cluster disappears from --ops -- but it does NOT remove the address temp, and because the short side is law-blocked the fix breaks the fake parity (O1306 -> O1305) and cascades misalignment into real 492 -> 703 with the multiset going 18t -> 19t. So the surplus is source-fixable and UNBANKABLE IN ISOLATION: it can only be taken together with a short-side fix that does not exist. @318 is diagnosed but unprobed: target emits ONE `li r17,0` serving both the byte store at 206(r31) and the live variable, ours emits two, so the target's source stores the variable rather than a fresh literal. (C) @bf4/@c14 address-PRE and the entry cluster are unchanged settled classes, and the entry cluster is newly shown to net to zero. DO NOT re-probe guard spellings at @144/@ab4/@bcc; DO NOT bank a surplus-side fix alone. The one genuinely open lever is a JOINT edit that removes a surplus instruction AND supplies a short-side instruction in the same probe, which no known law currently offers.
